newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols plummet, dealers confused.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols plummet, dealers confused.

text.p: An unexpected drop in implied volatility for dollar/mark options on Tuesday afternoon left over-the-counter (OTC) options dealers scrambling to identify the player.
Dollar/mark volatility began collapsing in late morning trade on Tuesday, despite continued mark weakness, which led some dealers to believe a large player or fund was affecting the entire curve.
"Somebody just whacked the mark curve in the last hour," said one OTC dealer, speaking at 1210 CST/1810 GMT. "The whole curve is nine (percent) flat right now."
Earlier in the session, implied volatility for one-month dollar/mark options was trading at 9.5 percent, dealers said.
"It doesn't make sense. I thought (volatilities) would go higher after spot broke through 1.5930 (marks)," said another dealer with an OTC firm.
"Somebody is selling quite a bit of vol across the whole curve," he speculated.
Another dealer, with a U.S. firm, said the sell-off may have begun in Chicago with the sale of 3,000 February $0.6300 mark futures put options, and then spread to the OTC market.
"I'm sure that whoever it was that was doing that did a lot more both on the floor and OTC," he said.
One trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said she believed the puts in question had been purchased by two firms two days earlier.
"They might have been rolling out of a position that they got in two days ago on expectations of touching, in dollar/mark, 1.60 even," she said.
The first dealer said it was also possible that the sell-off in volatility was technical, with multiple sell orders triggered above 1.5950 marks, a "swing point."

"If people are that nervous with their long positions, maybe spot is really directionally sensitive to 1.5950. If the positions in the market are large enough, it could be that sensitive to small movements in spot," he said.
However, he maintained that a single large player was a more likely theory.
"It feels like something big went through direct," a fourth dealer agreed.
In contrast to dollar/mark, one-month dollar/yen volatility was slightly higher just after noon at 8.5/8.7 percent compared with 8.55 percent early in the session.
Dealers said the dollar's move above 117 yen was sending jitters through the entire market.
